subject.title: Memory dreaming run pegs the gateway event loop for ~10 min until killed; short-term recall store can never persist (2026.6.9, reproduces on unmodified dist)

question: Should maintainers request and inspect the reporter's v2026.6.11 process sample before authorizing a fix PR, or is source-level evidence enough to start a bounded memory-core dreaming repair now?
rationale: The issue is clearly serious, but the source path is broad and current main has partial hardening without proof that pinpoints the late-run event-loop spin.

options.title: Request samples first
options.body: Ask for the three redacted process samples and corpus shape metrics, then queue a fix only after the hot frame is tied to a concrete current-main path.

options.title: Queue a guarded repair now
options.body: Start from the managed dreaming loop and add bounded pressure/yield behavior, accepting that the first PR may miss the specific final-phase stall.

options.title: Fold into broad pressure work
options.body: Treat this as dependent on the broader managed dreaming pressure fix and keep this issue as release-proof evidence until that fix lands and is verified.

recommendation.title: Request samples first
recommendation.body: Ask for the three redacted process samples and corpus shape metrics, then queue a fix only after the hot frame is tied to a concrete current-main path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core hardening and release-range context make this the best available routing owner for deciding whether proof is sufficient to start a repair.
